purpose: Human-reviewable plan consumed by Scripts/release_vegetation.py. Every number the placer uses is here so a reviewer can check the plan before an engine is ever launched. The instance transforms themselves live in the placement plan, which is generated by Scripts/create_vegetation.py and hashed here.

batching.note: A previous large import on this machine had to be run in groups to survive 16 GB. The plan ships pre-grouped by 400 m placement cell; -VegetationMaxBatches limits how many are placed per run and -VegetationResume carries the completed set forward.

instanceCapBasis: RTX 2070, 8 GB GDDR6, 1080p at 60 fps. Derived in the placement plan's budget block; this is the hard ceiling the placer refuses to cross whatever the plan says.

clearance.terrainMeshNote: THE TRAP. The 256 terrain tiles are 400 m squares whose AABBs are 400-800 m tall boxes enclosing the whole Temple. They are the ground the plants stand on and are never blockers. The placer counts how many actors it skipped for this reason and records the count, so a rename cannot silently turn the exclusion back on and re-create the 100 per cent false-blocker result.
clearance.unionNote: Hollow derived-union meshes have AABBs spanning +-8100 XY and Z 300..3425 that enclose the entire outer court. They are decomposed into their constituent boxes from source_elements_json and the recomposition is verified against expectedBoundsUnrealCm before the boxes are trusted, exactly as release_place_assets.py does.
clearance.mountEnclosureNote: No living plant inside the Mount enclosure ring or within the margin of it. Devarim 16:21. Every planned instance is re-tested against this ring in the editor before it is spawned, so a plan error cannot put a tree in the Azarah.
clearance.existingTreeNote: The 4265 retained illustrative OSM-derived trees are never touched. Their instance transforms are read numerically from the level and used as keep-out circles, which is a check only the editor can do because the offline generator has no access to their placed transforms.

lod.screenSizeRule: ScreenSize for the LOD that takes over at distance d is 2 * mesh bounds sphere radius / d, the standard perspective approximation at a 90 degree horizontal field of view. It is an approximation and is recorded as one; it should be tuned by eye once the meshes are in the level.

verification.note: After save and reopen the placer reads get_instance_count() off every component it created and requires it to equal the number of transforms it added. Runtime-added instance components are the risk in this whole scheme; this is the check that catches it if they do not persist.

limitations: Geometric placement only: no visual, collision, cook, performance or packaged acceptance is established.
Materials are created unassigned unless a material is already present at the expected path; assigning and tuning them is a separate reviewed step.
